newsitem.title: CANADA: FIGURE SKATING-ICE DANCERS BOURNE/KRAATZ WIN FIFTH TITLE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-ICE DANCERS BOURNE/KRAATZ WIN FIFTH TITLE.

text.p: Canadian ice dancers Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz won their fifth national title Sunday, bolstering their confidence that they can win world championship gold.
Like Canadian men's champ Elvis Stojko, Bourne and Kraatz are without equals in their own country.

This week's national championship in the German-born Kraatz's adopted hometown was, in the words of the current world bronze medallists, "a dry run" for the Champions Series Final coming up in two weeks and for the world championship in Lausanne, Switzerland in late March.

"It would be optimal at the Champions Series Final to beat (Russians) Krylova and Ovsiannikov since they were ahead of us last year," said Kraatz. "Then we would have only one team to worry about at worlds -- the world champions" -- Oksana Grischuk and Evgeny Platov.

Although France will also field two strong teams in Marina Anissina and Gwendal Peizerat and Sophie Moniotte and Pascal Lavanchy, the Canadians say they consider the Russians to be their main rivals for the season's marquee events.

"We know our competition. We know what we're capable of. It comes down to who has the best programmes, best technique, greatest expression. Everybody's very talented but we know now, that we're in the league," said Bourne.
Sunday afternoon at GM Place, the pair electrified the 16,000 fans with the programme they hope will put them atop the podium in Lausanne.
"Our freedance is very classy, it has a lot of emotions. It's fast, exciting and fun," said Bourne describing Sunday's performance set to music from the old movie "High Society."

"The first 20 seconds are so fast, it's insane. The second piece is very romantic -- a love story. Then we show a relaxed romantic side with the whistling piece and then we end with a bang. In the jive we want people to get up and join us.
"We're here to entertain, to put on a performance for the people. It's a major confidence builder to come to a national championship. For us it's a major warm-up for the next event."
For the last three weeks Bourne has been nursing an injured left heel. As soon as she sat down to wait for their marks -- a string of 5.8s and 5.9s -- Bourne removed her skate.
"The heel is swollen and throbbing," she said an hour later. "I iced it before we skated to numb it a bit."
The silver medal went to Chantal Lefebvre and Michel Brunet while Megan Wing and Aaron Lowe finished third.
Bourne and Kraatz will return Monday to their training site in Lake Placid, New York, where their famed Russian coach Natalia Dubova will help them prepare for the season's final challenges.
Sunday afternoon at the conclusion of the championship, Canada's 11-member world team was announced.

Travelling to Lausanne with Bourne and Kraatz will be Lefebvre and Brunet, men's competitors Elvis Stojko and Jeff Langdon, and the lone women's entry, Susan Humphreys, the newly crowned national champion.
In the pairs event, Canada will be represented by Marie-Claude Savard-Gagnon and Luc Bradet and Kristy Sargeant and Kris Wirtz.
